services.title: What The Vibe Company does
services.intro: Three ways to work together, the same three as on our homepage.

build.desc: We turn your need into a reliable product, in short cycles, all the way to production. Product and technical scoping, architecture, development, observability and documentation are all part of the job. We ship into secure production, working to GDPR and HDS requirements, then hand over to your teams.

operate.desc: We audit your workflows and measure the time actually spent, then we build the skills and connect your tools. Agents are deployed in your environment, securely, on the repetitive work. The result is measured in time your teams get back, and we keep improving it after go-live.

advise.desc: We help your company get the hang of AI: pick the use cases that create value, decide what to build and what to buy. Then we build an adoption roadmap that fits your organization. The training is hands-on, and we stay with your teams until the first use cases run in production.

edge.title: What makes us different
edge.intro: Projects in production, for clients with real constraints. Here are the numbers we can put our name to.

production.title: Products in production, not prototypes
production.desc: At Monka we took over the existing API and CRM, and in two months put into production the caregiver app, Lifeline (the CRM for their coordinating nurses) and the clinical engine. The caregiver assessment runs 165 questions, and the clinical framework has already gone through 12 versions without breaking the app. Since then we ship a new version roughly every two days.

agents.figureLabel: of LocService tickets answered with our AI drafts
agents.title: Agents that hold up at real volume
agents.desc: LocService handles several hundred support tickets a day. We read all their past tickets and internal documentation to draft the answer to every new one, connected to their internal APIs to pull the real customer context. Our drafts are used on 87% of tickets.

sectors.figureLabel: with AFP, on the MediaGen project
sectors.title: Demanding sectors: news, healthcare, food
sectors.desc: The Vibe Company is part of the technical consortium of MediaGen, AFP's France 2030 generative AI project, alongside Kairntech and Dawex: three tools for newsrooms in 24 months, with some components released under an open license. In healthcare, we work on encrypted, GDPR-compliant data for Monka. In food, we check Coup de Pates' product documents.

security.figureLabel: the requirements we work to in production
security.title: Security and operations are part of the delivery
security.desc: Health data hosting (HDS) and security are two things we know well, because our healthcare clients require it. We are also very strong on frontend and DevOps: the interface and the deployment pipeline are the same piece of work. We can hand over with documentation and runbooks, or keep running the product ourselves.

quivr.metaTitle: Quivr: open-source news search and monitoring
quivr.metaDescription: Quivr by The Vibe Company (YC W24): an open-source engine that follows news, emails and posts as they arrive, makes them searchable and alerts you on your topics.

hero.lead: Quivr follows news, emails and social posts as they arrive, makes them searchable in seconds, and alerts you when a topic you follow comes up.
hero.forWhom: Built for teams behind a newsroom tool, a media monitoring service or a research assistant.

flow.title: How Quivr works
flow.coreNote: Keeps every version · searches · watches your topics

benefits.title: Three things Quivr does for you

nothingLost.title: Nothing slips through
nothingLost.desc: Every article, email and post is kept, even when a service goes down. When an article is corrected, the earlier version stays readable.

meaning.title: Search by meaning, not just keywords
meaning.desc: Ask in your own words. Quivr finds articles on the same subject even when they use other words, and shows the exact passage it found.

alerts.title: Alerts that explain themselves
alerts.desc: Describe a topic once, in plain words. When a new article matches, even in other words or another language, Quivr tells your app why, so your team hears about it by email or in the app.

steps.alert: You save an alert: “harbour strike” with “ferry” or “port”.
steps.article: A feed you follow publishes “Harbour strike halts the ferry”.
steps.match: Quivr catches it and says why: “harbour strike” and “ferry” appear in the title and the text.
steps.correction: The article is then corrected. Quivr keeps both versions and tells you whether it still matches your alert.

mock.label: What it looks like
mock.headline: Harbour strike halts the ferry
mock.reason: Matched “harbour strike” in title, body; “ferry” in title, body.
mock.webhook: Signed webhook sent to your app
mock.correction: Correction received: new version kept, follow-up sent

problem.title: Content never stops arriving. Your monitoring can't drop any of it.
problem.intro: Press wires, mailboxes, X posts, RSS feeds: the content a newsroom tool, a media monitoring service or a research assistant follows keeps arriving, gets corrected, and is sometimes withdrawn. Searching it and following a topic over time takes more than a search box.

loss.title: Nothing lost on the way
loss.desc: Services go down; the stream does not wait. A document confirmed as received has to stay received, and be processed once the outage is over.

versions.title: Corrections without erasing history
versions.desc: Articles get corrected and withdrawn. You need the current text, the earlier one, and to know whether an alert still applies.

meaning.title: Found by keyword and by meaning
meaning.desc: An article on the same subject can use other words, or another language. Keyword search alone misses it.

features.title: Built for streams, not for a one-off index.

ingestion.title: Durable, idempotent ingestion
ingestion.desc: A write is acknowledged only once it is committed: an outage delays processing, it never loses content. Every write carries an idempotency key, so a replay returns the same result, and a correction creates a new immutable version instead of overwriting history.

search.title: Keyword and semantic search
search.desc: Lexical, semantic and hybrid search on Weaviate, with multilingual E5 embeddings. Text is searchable by keyword as soon as it is segmented; vectors arrive afterwards. Every hit names its document, its version and the exact passage.

alerts.title: Keyword and meaning alerts
alerts.desc: Save a query such as "harbour strike" AND (ferry OR port), or describe a subject in plain words to catch rephrased and translated articles. Every match records why it matched.

webhooks.title: Signed webhooks
webhooks.desc: When a new document matches an alert, Quivr sends a signed webhook (Standard Webhooks) to your receiver, retried for up to 24 hours by default. Your application can also follow every change through polling or SSE.

mcp.title: MCP for AI agents
mcp.desc: An AI agent such as Claude or Cursor searches your collections through MCP and cites the exact passage it quotes. The read profile only lists, searches and reads, no tool deletes, and the API key alone decides what the agent can read.

architecture.title: A generic core. Everything specific lives in plugins.
architecture.intro: The core stores, indexes and watches content, and stays generic. Formats, sources, AI models and business rules belong in plugins: small web services Quivr calls over HTTP, which you can swap or write yourself. Quivr ships a plugin for each job.
architecture.rule: Keep customer-specific formats and rules out of the core; they belong in plugins.
architecture.sourcesNote: Collected on a schedule, or pushed by a partner
architecture.coreNote: Go API and worker, one quivr binary
architecture.pluginsNote: Formats, sources, models, ranking and alert rules, over HTTP
architecture.outSearch: Search results, with their exact passage
architecture.outFeed: Change feed, by polling or SSE
architecture.selfHostDesc: Quivr runs next to your application, from one machine with Docker Compose to separate workers and a dedicated vector host. By default, document text goes nowhere outside your installation: the default plugins and the embedding model run there too.

rss.desc: Collects the articles of RSS, Atom and JSON feeds.

m365.desc: Collects the mail of a Microsoft 365 mailbox folder, with its attachments.

x.desc: Collects the posts of an X list and follows edits and deletions.
x.name: X lists

newsml.desc: Makes news agency items searchable, with their headlines and editorial metadata.

pdf.desc: Makes PDF files searchable, one passage per page. No OCR for scanned pages.

yours.name: Your plugin
yours.desc: A source, a format, a ranking or an alert rule, in any language that serves HTTP.

status.title: Evaluation stage. Not for production yet.
status.desc: The API is v0 and may change without notice, so do not run Quivr V2 in production yet. The local stack runs on Linux x86_64 and on Apple Silicon Macs, and there is no OCR: scanned documents stay unsearchable.
status.quickstartDesc: The Quickstart gets Quivr running on your machine in about fifteen minutes: add an article, search it, get an alert.

services.title: We deploy it for you
services.intro: Quivr V2 is free and self-hostable. When you want it running on your content, with your rules, The Vibe Company, the team that builds Quivr, does it with you as a service.

plugins.title: Business plugins
plugins.desc: Connectors for your sources, normalizers for your formats, alert rules for your domain. Written as plugins, so your specifics never fork the core.

production.title: Going to production
production.desc: Installation on your infrastructure, sizing for your volumes, upgrades and monitoring. Quivr V2 is still in evaluation: we tell you plainly what is ready for your case and what is not.

security.title: Security and HDS
security.desc: Hosting that fits your constraints, working to HDS requirements for health data, with scoped API keys and verified TLS on outgoing connections. Text stays in your installation unless you turn on a plugin that calls an outside service.

history.title: From Quivr V1 to Quivr V2

v1.label: V1 · 2023
v1.title: An open-source RAG “second brain”
v1.desc: Quivr started in 2023 as an open-source RAG engine to build your second brain with generative AI. It became one of the most followed projects on GitHub, with {stars} stars, went through Y Combinator (W24), then focused on customer support.

tvc.title: Quivr becomes The Vibe Company
tvc.desc: The founders stopped Quivr as their company's direction to build The Vibe Company, an AI-native agency. The repository stayed open source.

v2.label: V2 · today
v2.title: A new engine for content streams
v2.desc: Quivr V2 replaced the V1 code base on main: an engine in Go for durable ingestion, search and monitoring, built by The Vibe Company and still under the MIT license.

history.communityDesc: The V1 code is preserved at the v1-final tag, the last commit of Quivr V1 before V2 replaced it on main. Read it, fork it or run it from there.
history.storyLink: Read the story: from Quivr to The Vibe Company

v1.a: Quivr V2 replaced the V1 code base on the main branch. V1 is preserved at the v1-final tag, the last commit of Quivr V1, so you can still read, fork or run it from there.

license.a: MIT. It is free to use, modify and self-host. Some plugins rely on libraries with their own license, such as pypdf (BSD-3-Clause) for the PDF plugin.

production.q: Can I use Quivr V2 in production?
production.a: Not yet. Quivr V2 is at the evaluation stage and its API is v0, which may change without notice. Try it on your machine with the Quickstart, and talk to us if you want to plan a production rollout.

selfHost.a: Yes. Quivr runs on servers you control, next to your application: one machine with Docker Compose to evaluate it, or a deployment with separate workers and a dedicated vector host. By default, Quivr itself sends document text nowhere outside your installation.

support.a: For questions and bugs, use the issues and discussions of the GitHub repository. For business plugins, planning a production rollout, or hosting that works to HDS requirements for health data, The Vibe Company can help as a service: book a call.
